correctness.rationale: Exact stationary mass ratios reconstruct the generator by detailed balance. Consecutive-ratio division gives the product \(F_k(a)F_{n-k}(b)\). The explicit positive difference for every integer \(j\ge2\) isolates both boundary constraints; the limit \(F_j(u)	o1\) and \(F_1(u)\le1\iff u\ge1/3\) prove the population-uniform threshold. In symmetric cases, ratios \(R_0,R_1\), strict decreasing interior ratios, and reflection prove peaks. The monotone equation for \(u_n\), its location, and first-order asymptotic are checked analytically. The stand-alone exact checker corroborated 114964 finite assertions; finite tests do not prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: For a concrete autocatalytic stochastic chemistry count law, the result determines exact finite-population stationary shape for all positive rate parameters, a sharp mutation threshold uniform over arbitrarily large populations, and a distinct endpoint-peak versus log-concavity transition. This identifies mathematically different concentration regimes that simple unimodality or mixing cutoff results do not characterize. The result is complete for the natural invariant count law rather than a numerical one-off.
